pr_title: Scoping CSS keyframes in emulated view encapsulation
pr_body:
Keyframes are not scoped for `Emulated` view encapsulated component, practically making them global and causing css leakage

> note: this does not happen with the `shadowDom` view encapsulation, there there is no leakage 

Since keyframes are not hierarchical I don't believe this issue can be solved without modifying the keyframes names, so the only thing possible I believe is to actually rename the keyframes using the component's scope selector,

The way I did it is by scanning the css twice, in the first scan I modified/scoped the keyframes names in the way mentioned above and in the second I updated animation rules using such keyframes

> Note: animations using keyframes not defined in the file are not modified, still allowing global keyframes to be defined

I understand that this is changing the actual names of the keyframes so it may not be what we actually want here, but I figured that opening a PR and starting a discussion would not hurt

## What is the current behavior?
Issue Number: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/33885

Currently keyframes are not scoped so, if I create two different keyframe animations in two different components but with the same name, those will clash and only one of them will be applied to both components

You can see it in this example I created: [demo](https://angular-keyframes-leak-demo.netlify.app/) [code](https://github.com/dario-piotrowicz/angular-keyframes-leak-demo)

What happens is that I have two different components each with a keyframes called `box-animation` which colors the component's background, as you can see the application does not behave as expected:
![Screenshot at 2021-06-20 16-58-37](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61631103/122680918-a160e880-d1e9-11eb-9ee2-cf6205bc2f67.png)


## What is the new behavior?

Keyframes are scoped so that they include the component's scope selector like so:
![Screenshot at 2021-06-20 16-55-49](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61631103/122680701-6d38f800-d1e8-11eb-91d3-4099be31b36c.png)

and this allows the keyframes to remain isolated:
![Screenshot at 2021-06-20 16-59-02](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61631103/122680945-c0f81100-d1e9-11eb-8069-05868a3a3710.png)

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No 
(at least I don't think so)

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->


## Other information

As I mentioned this will cause all the keyframes names in components with the `Emulated` view encapsulation to be modified, this is definitely not too nice/elegant but I think it's the only way to scope the keyframes and I believe that it is still better to leave them global as they are now (as that produces unwanted css leakage + it is inconsistent with what happens with `ShadowDom`)
pr_comments: For other reviewers, I checked through the Angular animations code, which also makes use of `@keyframes` but this does not seem to be affected by this change, since it always generates its own keyframe names, and does not reference ones in the component definition.

**TO DO:** make sure css variables are taken into consideration/theirs values are not scoped (as they can end with `animation` or `animation-name`)
> as mentioned in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/42608#discussion_r671813128

___

based on the [specs](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-variables-1/#custom-property) the possible variable names are [dashed-ident](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#typedef-dashed-ident) which I believe are basically [custom-ident](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/custom-ident)s starting with `"--"`

So they (besides the initial `"--"`) can contain:
- any alphabetical character (A to Z, or a to z),
- any decimal digit (0 to 9),
- a hyphen (`-`),
- an underscore (`_`),
- an escaped character (preceded by a backslash, `\`),
- a Unicode character (in the format of a backslash, `\`, followed by one to six hexadecimal digits, representing its Unicode code point)

What do you think?

Just to clarify, I was thinking of something of the sort:

> A Keyframe could for example be: `@keyframes "strange \" keyframe name"`
> and then a css could have: `animation-name: "strange \" keyframe name"`
> or even: `animation-name: 'strange " keyframe name'`

So handling such escaped quotes wouldn't be as simple as substituting them with a placedholder and handling them that way, as we'd also need to consider them and also handle their unescaped version.
So this would sort of need both a placeholder strategy (so that they don't interfere with the normal regexes) and a strategy to handle them unescaped

It could be quite tricky to get right and lots of effort for something really edge case (considering that chrome doesn't even seem to support strings at this point)

On the other hand it is sort of standard to be able to escape quotes in strings, so not handling that would make this less then ideal....

Can I suggest the following wording for the commit message?


> fix(compiler): scope css keyframes in emulated view encapsulation 
> 
> Ensure that keyframes rules, defined within components with emulated view encapsulation,
> are scoped to avoid collisions with keyframes in other components.
> 
> This is achieved by renaming these keyframes to add a prefix that makes them unique across
> the application.
> 
> Closes #33885
> 
> BREAKING CHANGE:
> 
> Keyframes names are now prefixed with the component's "scope name".
> For example, the following keyframes rule in a component definition, whose "scope name"
> is `host_my_cmp`:
> 
> ```css
> @keyframes foo { ... }
> ```
> 
> will become:
> 
> ```
> @keyframes host_my_cmp-foo { ... }
> ```
> 
> Any TypeScript/JavaScript code which relied on the names of keyframes rules
> will no longer match.
> 
> The recommended solution in this case is to:
> - define keyframes rules in global stylesheets (e.g `styles.css`)
> - define keyframes rules programmatically in code.
>

> fix(compiler): scope css keyframes in emulated view encapsulation

Hello everyone, I just fixed the issue locally (I've tested it both in serve and build modes)

Since keyframes are not hierarchical I don't believe this issue can't be solved without modifying the keyframes names, so the only thing possible I believe is to actually rename the keyframes using the host selector, I did so by prepending the host selector to the keyframes names like so:
![Screenshot at 2021-06-19 22-23-01](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61631103/122655766-f569bf80-d14c-11eb-9f02-4e96f311bf2d.png)

The way I did it is by scanning the css twice, in the first scan I modified/scoped the keyframes names in the way mentioned above and in the second I updated animation rules using such keyframes 
> note: animations containing keyframes not declared in the scoped file are not modified, allowing the use of globally defined keyframes too

Please let me know if mine is an acceptable solution and if that's the case, could I please be assigned to the issue so that I can implement the same for the AOT compiler and create a PR for the fix? 

( Also if my solution is not acceptable for some reason please let me know and I will be happy to discuss and change my solution accordingly )

> ps: this issue is only relative to components with the emulated view encapsulation, the shadow dom view encapsulation does not create such issue (so I believe that this should be fixed even if only for the sake of consistency)
Thanks for looking at this, its quiet an old issue now, but as you say its still not fixed, I think the stackblitz expired

I actually finished working on it and created a PR, I hope you don't mind :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye: 

(worst case scenario, if my solution is not ok, the PR will just be rejected)
